title: Mitigating Social Bias in English and Urdu Language Models Using PRM-Guided Candidate Selection and Sequential Refinement
findings: The paper does not provide findings specific to religion, as results were aggregated across all sociocultural categories (gender, ethnicity, religion, etc.). The general findings indicate that the baseline Urdu model completions were substantially more biased than the English ones. However, the proposed inference-time debiasing methods, PRM-Select (best-of-N sampling) and PRM-Sequential (iterative refinement), significantly reduced this bias in both languages, demonstrating their effectiveness in mitigating stereotypical associations, including those related to religion.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the generation of biased or stereotypical single-word completions in response to prompts involving socially sensitive contexts, which included the category of religion. Specifically, it assessed stereotypical associations such as those between religion and violence.
